id: DS-DEF-2::Beasts & Monsters: plagued, perimeter AND organized force::v2
text: Defense at {settlement} is not an emergency arrangement, it is the week's work: the rotations run, the gates close on time, and nobody treats any of it as unusual.
{settlement} kept no defence because the country never asked for one, and the country is asking now; the town is improvising what it never built.
Nothing at {settlement} was organized against the country, and the threat now at hand has found the gap.
You find {settlement} with nothing organised against what has come out of the country, and people arming themselves with whatever is at hand.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: walls AND professional garrison::v2
text: Approaching {settlement}, you see the walls and the soldiers who belong on them, and any attacker would think again about the cost.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: walls AND professional garrison::v3
text: People at {settlement} believe the town could be held, and the soldiers on the walls give them good reason to.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: walls with NO force::v1
text: {settlement} has walls and nobody to put on them. A determined attacker takes this town with ladders and patience, and requires nothing else.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: walls with NO force::v3
text: People at {settlement} admit it when asked: the town has walls and nobody to stand on them.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: walls with NO force::v4
text: {settlement}'s walls are kept by its watch and nobody else, which is enough to see who comes and goes and nothing like enough to hold them.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: walls with NO force::v5
text: The only people on {settlement}'s walls are the watch on their rounds, and everyone knows that would not stop an army.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: walls with NO force::v6
text: {settlement} had nobody to put on its walls until the siege came; the people on them now are townsfolk who have never held a wall before.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: neither walls nor force::v5
text: With trouble at hand, {settlement} has no wall to close and nobody trained to send, and each household is deciding for itself whether to stay.
The town could go through a bad season with its arrangements intact, and the people who would have to be paid through one know it.
Visitors to {settlement} are told which few streets to avoid, and the advice turns out to be right.
Everyone entering {settlement} is counted at the gate by a soldier whose job it is, and counted again on the way out.
{settlement} has no organized force. Defense here is individual armed citizens, with no command, no training and no way to coordinate a response.
If {settlement} were attacked, its people would fight with no leaders and no plan, each household for itself.
Nobody at {settlement} is responsible for defending the town; ask who is, and nobody can name anyone.
{settlement} kept no defenders of its own, and the people defending it now are neighbours who stepped forward when the trouble came.
There was never a force at {settlement}; whoever leads the defence now is learning the work as the trouble goes on.
No dependable road, river or port reaches {settlement}, and the town gets by on its own: enough for an ordinary year, with little to spare.

id: DS-ECO-1::COMBINATION C4: a low rung on a working approach::v2
text: Some trade comes past {settlement}, and little of it stops. The town is poor, and its people say so to anyone who asks.

id: DS-ECO-1::COMBINATION C4: a low rung on a working approach::v3
text: {settlement}'s market sells little, though the {access} is busy; most of the traffic does not stop, and the traders here are poor.

id: DS-ECO-1::COMBINATION C4: a low rung on a working approach::v6
text: There is no market at {settlement} to hold the trade that passes by, and the town stays poor while the trade goes on its way.
Some petty theft goes on here, and some trading without a licence. It is a nuisance, nothing more.

id: DS-ECO-9::HOW THE NEED IS MET: much of it brought in::v1
text: Food carts come into {settlement} most days, and they matter: a good part of what the town eats is grown elsewhere and brought in.

id: DS-ECO-9::HOW THE NEED IS MET: much of it brought in::v2
text: {settlement} grows only part of what it eats; the rest comes in from the farms around it and from trade.
{settlement} has goods to sell, but the way out is unreliable, and a trader never knows whether a load will get through.
Faith carries real weight in {settlement}'s money. What the religious houses take in and spend is a large part of the town's business.
The religious houses at {settlement} are among its biggest buyers and employers, and a bad year for them is a bad year for the town.
Market day is when {settlement} fills: the roads bring buyers, and the stalls are there for them.
{settlement}'s market lives off through-traffic; the town sells to the road as much as to itself.
The market stands where carts always stopped; stalls followed the carts, and {settlement} grew around them.
{settlement}'s market handles more than the town could ever use; the difference is the town's living.
No market or fair stands in {settlement}: what trade the town does is done house to house and on the road.
A traveller passing through {settlement} can change coin, borrow or settle a debt at the town's bank without carrying the silver home.

id: DS-GEN-13::COMMERCE: a merchant guild, no bank::v2
text: {settlement}'s merchant guild sets the terms of trade and its members carry the town's dealings outward.

id: DS-GEN-13::COMMERCE: a merchant guild, no bank::v4
text: An outside trader at {settlement} either accepts its merchant guild's terms or sells to the guild's members at their price.

id: DS-GEN-13::COMMERCE: craft guilds, no merchant guild::v4
text: A newcomer with a trade at {settlement} must be taken on by its guild before they can work here.
Goods wait in {settlement}'s warehouses between the road and the buyer until the price is right.
{settlement}'s warehouses fill after the harvest and empty through the year as the town trades out of them.
A trader at {settlement} can rent warehouse space and leave goods there between journeys.
{settlement} pays wages for its defense as well as keeping its walls, and the money is found every season.
Robed monks and nuns are a common sight on the way into {settlement}.
Anyone new to {settlement} who needs a meal or a bed is sent to the monks.
Decisions at {settlement} are slow because the whole {seat} must agree, and once made they are rarely undone.
At {settlement} the town's business goes to the whole {seat}, and everybody has learned how long the answer takes.
The {seat} at {settlement} has left obvious decisions untaken because its members cannot agree on them.
The trading houses at {settlement} pay for their own armed guards, a private army that keeps order wherever the houses do business. Where the guards and the {seat} disagree, the guards usually win.

id: DS-POW-6::capture pressure ADVANCING (weak security, poor prosperity)::v8
text: A watch walks {settlement}'s streets, but the danger is in the hall, where officials paid next to nothing are worth buying.
A share of what arrives at {settlement} never appears at the gate, and the share is not small.

id: DS-POW-6::GM ADVISORY: the commander is a political actor::v3
text: {faction} answers to the {seat} at {settlement} in name only: whatever the {seat} plans needs its consent, and that consent is bargained for.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: neither walls nor force::v10
text: {settlement} lies open on every side; its watch keeps to its rounds while the danger everyone talks about is close.
You can see that {settlement}'s defenders are armed and equipped from the town's own trades; you can also see that they eat no better than anyone else.
Those who keep order at {settlement} walk in pairs now, and there are lanes they no longer walk at all.
{settlement}'s soldiers are paid by the season and drilled by the week, whether or not anything comes.
{settlement} had nobody whose work was its defence before the army came, so the siege is being held by householders taking turns.
At {settlement} you find the guards posted where the newcomers camp, not at the edges of the place.
{settlement}'s people under arms are too few to cover its {defwork}, and the town spends on the {defwork} before it spends on them.
{settlement} is large enough that anyone arriving expects a wall around it, and is surprised to walk straight in from open country.
{settlement} lived off its {good} and little else, and the {good} has failed; there is nothing else to turn to.
{settlement} has several kinds of goods to sell outward, and the siege has shut every one of them in.
Half of this trade was always done elsewhere, and with the siege closing the roads, the half the town does has nowhere to go.

id: DS-ECO-12::CRITICAL IMPORT: a house needs what the land lacks::v4
text: {settlement} has no {good} of its own, and the siege lets none in, so the work that needs it is stopping.

id: DS-ECO-12::CRITICAL IMPORT: the land cannot give it::v4
text: {settlement} neither grows nor buys any {good}; people there do without.
{settlement} spends on its faith without keeping a house for it, so a quarrel over the rites would be felt in its money first.
{settlement} is running short of {good}, and the siege lets none in.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: walls AND professional garrison::v1
text: {settlement}'s garrison roll puts paid soldiers on every stretch of its walls, so raiders stay away and an army would pay dearly; a long siege would be another matter.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: neither walls nor force::v4
text: {settlement} has no line and no force, and the threat now at hand has noticed both.

id: DS-DEF-2::Invasion & War: neither walls nor force::v6
text: You find {settlement} open on every side, with nobody posted anywhere, while the danger everyone talks about is close.
{settlement} is cut off now, and what its food trades salted and dried before the siege is what stands between the town and hunger.
The town's count of its stores at {settlement} covers an ordinary year and no more, so one bad harvest would leave it short before spring.
{settlement}'s {defwork} was short of hands before the siege; now everyone who can hold a weapon has a place on it, and most of them are learning as they go.
{settlement} has nobody whose work it is to stand on its {defwork}, though the town keeps the {defwork} in repair.
{settlement} keeps its {defwork} in repair before it pays anyone to stand guard there, and the few who do turn out are stretched thin.

id: DS-ECO-1::COMBINATION C4: a low rung on a working approach::v1
text: Traffic moves along {settlement}'s {access} every day, and little of its money stays behind.
{settlement} is fed, but only just. A poor harvest is felt at every table; a good one means a little put by.
People in {settlement} work at more than one trade, so a bad year for one is not a bad year for everyone.
The town has taken this trade as far as it goes, from the ground to the finished thing.

id: DS-ECO-12::CRITICAL IMPORT: a house needs what the land lacks::v3
text: {settlement}'s {institution} has had no {good} since the siege closed the roads, and its work has stopped or soon will.
Faith carries real weight in {settlement}'s money, though the place keeps no house for it: what its people give for their faith leaves with them on the feast days.
At {settlement} the feast days set the calendar of buying and selling, and the offerings leave the place with the people who carry them.
Visitors find {settlement}'s market without asking; the busiest street through town leads straight to it.
Paid hands keep {settlement} safe; the town does not trust to luck and neighbours.
{settlement}'s {institution} is short of what it needs from upstream, though the building and the skilled hands are all still there.
The {seat} at {settlement} worries less about rivals than about the town turning on it.

id: DS-POW-6::capture pressure ADVANCING (weak security, poor prosperity)::v7
text: {settlement}'s watch keeps the streets, but nobody keeps an eye on the officials, and they are paid too little to refuse a purse.
Goods reach {settlement} around the customs rather than through them. The cargo lists are false, the landing places are unofficial, and the duties the town should collect are never paid.
The customs at {settlement} keep proper books, and a good share of goods goes around them anyway.
